verdict.rationale: The evidence shows a published third-party designee path for EIN applications that requires signed authorization from the responsible party, and a credentialed Authorized e-file Provider role. It also indicates that signatures on mobile-friendly forms such as Form 15620 stay with the taxpayer through Online Account and ID.me biometric sign-in. This is fragmentary, not a consolidated published rulebook of what a third party may and may not do. Missing for 10: general authorization forms (e.g., a power-of-attorney or information-authorization form), an explicit scope of designee permissions and prohibitions, a consolidated roles taxonomy, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: a third-party designee may apply, with signed authorization from the responsible party
Online Account (OLA) is required to complete mobile friendly forms that require signatures
You'll need an account with ID.me to sign in to access your tax information and use services on IRS.gov.
it can take up to 45 days from the date of submission for the IRS to approve your e-file application
